u08-rem-mid.resolution: I checked each flag against the Greek and found no meaning error. οὐ μόνον ἀρχικήν τινος οὐδὲ ἑνὸς τὴν ἀρχὴν ἀλλὰ κοινήν contrasts individual rule with a shared kingdom: 'not merely the rule of someone, nor the rule of one, but common'. 'It is not the rule of some one person or of a single ruler, but a common kingdom' keeps that contrast; μόνον here sharpens 'someone's' and does not open a 'not only … but also' that would make the kingdom both individual and common. 'The right to sit … and judge' supplies the noun English needs for the articular infinitive τὸ … καθεζομένους κρίνειν. 'Ps 129,1b.2', 'Ps 131,6', 'Ps 131,15-17' etc. are the edition's fragment lemmata in LXX numbering, not translation references. Θήραν/σίτησιν 'one … another renders' follows the Greek, which does not name the translators. The remaining points (supplied 'he', passives, 'decree' for βουλήν, 'out of love', particles) are idiom with the same sense.
